note: The pgmvox port of Riftwater (freeform/lib/ports/riftwater) written as ordered layer operations. Not executable; every parameter was read from the port's scripts, and the library calls keep their pgmvox names. `lib` names the pgmvox function the port calls today; `local` marks code the port wrote itself; `new` means no pgmvox op or studio concept of that name exists. class A = layer operation, B = library entry + placement, C = made. The group order is the requested one; the script runs ground, volume, buildings, stalls, dressing, mirror, objectives.stamp, so the monument `box` is resolved against the finished ground only in `stamps.objectives`.

ground.gap: Local code (plan._rift_edge) in the port. No pgmvox op makes an island outline with one ragged lip held straight at named bands; nearest is landform.coast or the studio's relief 'rim' mark.
Formula in plan.land(); pgmvox.noise supplies smoothstep and fbm. The studio's relief marks (point, line, area, scarp) state the same shapes as placed marks.
fbm lattices are sized to the red-half grid (120 x 176): the seeds reproduce only in an interpreter that implements this noise on this grid.
An asymmetric valley shaped before the watercourse op cuts the channel: banks 7 vs 14 blocks, per-reach level. landform.watercourse has a symmetric bank and picks its own levels.
Local in the port; lake() covers the ellipse, the spit and the outlet disc are not parameters.
landform.scarp is a cliff that jumps to half its height at the line (PORT-REPORT); a ridge whose foot wanders over fifteen blocks is a new landform.
